answer: The main theorem says that one deterministic Turing machine, with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, multiplies two n-bit integers exactly in O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)) worst-case time, with kappa = 2^-182. The wiki calls this model a kepikir. The result refutes the Sikited, the claim that n log n is the best possible order of growth for multiplying two integers on that model. The proof plan is: (1) build two power-saving tape procedures, an address-chunk interchange and a sifigeg, from fixed linear networks; (2) use them to speed up the synthetic transforms and the ring convolution; (3) use Sikusup and Bluestein chirps to turn prime-length transforms into power-of-two ones, leaving permutations inside the transform identities rather than executing them; (4) assemble the exact 2n-bit product from radix digits, with total error below 1/2 so rounding recovers the exact integers; (5) total the cost after dividing by the volume, and show that a power of log n is saved.

key_idea.statement: Each recursive call works on streams of 1/W of the volume and makes fewer than W times m smaller calls, so the cost per unit volume grows by less than a factor m when the parameter grows by a factor m; that leaves a power of the parameter below one as the total cost.

stuck.quote: Beating that needs cheaper address movement and cheaper butterfly arithmetic
stuck.note: The page says the log factor can only be beaten by cheaper address movement and cheaper butterfly arithmetic. I could see that n log n comes from scanning n bits at each of log n layers, but not why these two are the only levers, or why cheaper address movement removes the log factor. I accepted the claim without seeing the link.

stuck.quote: The recursion gets its strict inequality $s<Wm$ from [Pukezad](dol)
stuck.note: I went to the Pukezad page for the strict inequality and followed the rank count as written. I could not see how s<Wm turns the unrolled recurrence into the bound O(V f^tau). I followed the steps without seeing why the ratio s/W below m makes the geometric sum behave like a power of f below one.

stuck.quote: A call at parameter $mf$, with $m=10^6$ the label-space dimension
stuck.note: Here m is the fixed number 10^6, but the page later uses only m < 2^20 and an exponent margin. I could not tell whether the bound is claimed for this particular m or for every m, and I took it as the former.

The exponent 1 - 2^-50 is asserted, and the margin is checked with an exp and tangent argument and the rationals 339/22587335000000 and 73/19906842167500, which I did not recompute. I accepted that s/W is below m^tau from the stated bounds.

The label spaces are built inside a tensor power F^{tensor 3}, and tensor products are outside my background. I could not decode the label construction, so I followed the rank arithmetic by its stated numbers only.

The page uses tilde and script variants of the transform (the computed and exact counterparts, with output map and scaling). I could not tell how the computed object relates to the exact one until I read the following sentence, and I could not tell the status of the exactness equality it asserts.

I accepted that the source permutation drops out because an identity holds, which the sentence attributes to the zom page. I did not open that page, so this step rests on the sentence alone, and I was guessing that the identity is proved there.
I accepted that the error on the coefficients is below 1/2, so that rounding is exact, without opening the mes page. The claim that rounding gives exact integers is a statement I did not check.

reason: I am confident of the model, the conjecture and the statement of the main result, which the front page, the kepikir page, the Sikited page and the main result page state directly. I am moderately confident of the plan: I followed the outline on the front page and read the pipozop, pegapev, tobifup, totipuv, divogam and Pukezad pages, which give the reasons in outline. I did not verify the cost exponent (Dedapov page), the error bound (Nutipib page) or the permutation identity (Nizizag page). I used 10 of the 15 allowed page openings. The weakest points are the chains that explain why the saving takes the form s/W < m, and why the fast address movement removes the log factor.
